Markets.title: DIIs increase stake in 8 midcap stocks in Q2FY27
Markets.summary: During the September 2026 quarter, Domestic Institutional Investors increased their holdings in eight NSE midcap stocks by over 200 basis points. These companies included Swiggy, One97 Communications, Meesho, Cochin Shipyard, Lenskart Solutions, Piramal Finance, APL Apollo Tubes, and SBI Cards and Payment Services.

Markets.title: Bajaj Finance Q2 preview: Profit may jump 29%, NII 24% as strong loan growth lifts earnings
Markets.summary: Bajaj Finance expects a 29% jump in net profit and a 24% rise in net interest income for the July-September quarter, driven by strong loan demand. However, analysts warn that rising borrowing costs may create pressure on the company's lending margins.

Markets.title: FPI selling crosses Rs 52,000 crore in October as Nifty defies foreign exodus
Markets.summary: Foreign portfolio investors withdrew over Rs 52,000 crore from Indian equities in October due to rising US Treasury yields and high crude oil prices. Despite this massive foreign exodus, benchmark indices Nifty and Sensex rebounded sharply, driven by strong domestic institutional buying and gains in the IT sector.

Markets.title: Jefferies’ Chris Wood says it’s time to diversify beyond AI. Where should investors look now?
Markets.summary: Jefferies analyst Chris Wood advises investors to reduce heavy exposure to artificial intelligence stocks due to slowing earnings growth and high valuations. Instead, he recommends reallocating capital toward semiconductor companies, India, China, and other Asian markets.

Markets.title: FPIs pull out Rs 52,100 cr from equities in Oct so far amid global headwinds
Markets.summary: Foreign portfolio investors withdrew Rs 52,100 crore from Indian equities in October following a Rs 35,861 crore outflow in September. This financial retreat was driven by elevated crude oil prices, higher US bond yields, and a stronger dollar.

Markets.title: Mcap of nine of top-10 most valued firms surges by Rs 3.65 lakh cr; TCS shines
Markets.summary: Last week, the market valuation of nine out of the top ten most valued Indian firms surged by Rs 3.65 lakh crore, driven by strong gains in the BSE Sensex and Nifty. TCS, Bharti Airtel, and Infosys led these gains, while Larsen & Toubro was the only firm among the top ten to report a decline in valuation.
